text.title: SDD Promotion Gate Checklist Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules grounding the sdd-promotion-gate-checklist methodology, covering both lifecycle gates it owns. Each rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale. The terminal `skip-this-methodology` rule is the safety valve invoked by the decision tree when preconditions fail.

section.title: Background: the two gates
section.p: The promotion-gate methodology gates TWO lifecycle transitions. The `backlog → todo` gate is covered by 01-04 + 06. The `in-progress → done` gate is delegated to the readiness-checklist methodology and enforces additional quality gates.
Additional quality-gate items enforced at the done gate:

list.item: API tests pass — REQUIRED when the feature touched backend code (any file under backend source tree).
Playwright positive AND negative cases pass — REQUIRED when the feature has a user-facing flow.
Surface-coupling check — REQUIRED when the feature added a new public surface (skill trigger, API path, CLI flag, exported name).

section.reference: Canonical 10-item readiness checklist; this gate consumes it.

rule.statement: Every checklist item MUST be binary (yes/no, file exists, link returns 200).
rule.rationale: Subjective criteria turn the gate into gut-feel and erode trust.

rule.statement: Checklist MUST verify presence of spec.md (always) + plan.md (unless skip-criteria met per plan-md-structure) before backlog→todo promotion.
rule.rationale: Missing canonical artefacts prevent task generation and downstream wave-planning.

rule.statement: Checklist MUST name the reviewer signing off; '@team' is forbidden.
Checklist MUST enumerate open blockers; any non-empty list blocks promotion.
rule.rationale: Hidden blockers surface in in-progress and stall sprints.

rule.statement: Each `yes` MUST link to file / PR / decision URL.
For `in-progress → done` transitions, this methodology delegates to `readiness-checklist`. The readiness.md file MUST exist and every item ticked with evidence before the feature can be moved.
rule.rationale: The done-gate has 10 items with conditional applicability (API tests, Playwright, UI heuristics). Replicating that logic here would drift; single source of truth lives in readiness-checklist.

rule.statement: The reviewer MUST verify which conditionals apply by inspecting the git diff, NOT by accepting the developer's self-assessment.
rule.rationale: The author has a blind spot for what counts as "user-facing" or "public surface". The diff is the source of truth.

rule.statement: Author MUST stop and route elsewhere when the decision-tree resolves to a skip leaf; partial application of this methodology against an unfit input is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Forcing the methodology onto a mismatched input produces low-quality artefacts and erodes trust in the corpus.
